title: Spotlight claims & rhythm notes — Amar Patel
content:
Quick context:
This is my micro-scratchpad for the coming manager cadence (monthly sync + quarterly check). Raw, short-form. Purpose: 1) surface 3 concise claims I want to own in the next 6–12 weeks, 2) draft the one-on-one agenda + timing, 3) prepare compact evidence bullets and possible asks.

Spotlight claims (short, defensible) — pick 3
1) "Deliver predictable onboarding for Dedicated customers" — reduce mean time to first inference by 30% via runbook + onboarding templates.
   - Why it matters: onboarding friction drives churn and support load; predictable TTFI supports faster revenue recognition.
   - Quick evidence to cite: onboarding pilot with AcmeCorp reduced manual steps from 9 -> 4 (summary email 2026-01-28).
   - Risk / unknowns: resource constraints on infra-led fixes; need SRE time for infra automation.

2) "Create lightweight evaluation pack for runtime regressions" — 20 minute workflow to verify perf/quality before rollout.
   - Why: past rollout caused 8% latency regressions unnoticed until prod.
   - Evidence: postmortem notes (rollout-2025-11) and two incidents where rollback saved customers.
   - Quick ask: 1 week of applied-ml QA time + product signoff.

3) "Own a repeatable career conversation framework for ICs" — shorten promotion prep cycles by giving compossible evidence templates.
   - Why: saves managers time and increases fairness/transparency.
   - Evidence: pilot with 2 managers (Feb) increased candidate readiness.
   - Ask: copy of comp template shipped to PeopleOps playbook.

One-on-one agenda (20–30m) — proposed rhythm
- 0–3m: check-in (mood, blockers) — quick signal (one sentence)
- 3–10m: highlights since last sync (2 bullets) — wins + asymmetric risk
- 10–18m: focus claim deep-dive (pick 1 claim) — evidence + needs (concrete asks)
- 18–24m: career signal / development micro-step (ask manager for 1 micro-feedback)
- 24–30m: wrap + confirmations (who does what)

Evidence bullets (keeps short, copyable)
- "Onboarding: reduced manual checklist steps from 9->4; demo runbooks created; trial customer pipeline conversion +12% month over month"
- "Runtime eval: test harness added to CI for 2 models; latency regression alert runbook used in 2 incidents"
- "Career convos: pilot templates used by 2 managers; candidate prep time down 40% for those pilots"

Ask scripts (one-liners to use in meeting)
- "Can you allocate one SRE sprint for the onboarding automation so we can remove that manual step?"
- "If we prioritize the runtime eval pack, I can own rollout and save us from repeated rollbacks — can I get a week of QA time?"
- "I'd like your endorsement on the promotion evidence template so I can publish it to managers next week. Any objections?"

Manager cues (things I want them to say/hear)
- "This is useful — let's scope the SRE work and confirm in the next planning meeting."
- "I back you on leading the eval pack; escalate any cross-team blockers to me."
- "I can give a concrete micro-feedback for your career piece by next Monday."

Notes to self (messy, quick)
- Keep claims measurable. Replace vague verbs ("help", "improve") with target numbers or deliverables.
- When manager pushes back on resourcing: present low-effort MVP + follow-up milestones.
- Prep 1 pager (one side) for each claim: 3 lines of context, 3 bullets of evidence, 1 clear ask.

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm SRE availability: ping SRE lead (Elena) for capacity in April.
- Consolidate pilot evidence (emails + dashboards) into a single attachment for manager.
- Draft promotion evidence template and send to Mira for early feedback.

Micro-rituals (daily/weekly habits to keep claims moving)
- Monday: 15m triage (update evidence list + status)
- Wednesday: 10m check with owners (SRE / Applied ML / Managers)
- Friday: 20m write/update the one-pager for claim in progress

Stuff to copy-paste into a calendar invite (meeting description)
- "Agenda: 1) quick check-in (1-2 lines); 2) one claim deep-dive (10m): progress + asks; 3) career signal (5m); 4) next steps. Please bring one data point you want feedback on."

Unresolved / friction/ guardrails
- I tend to overload manager agenda — be explicit about what I want them to decide.
- Keep the meeting lean: if we need asynchronous review, send one-pager ahead of time.
- Avoid bringing more than 2 asks per meeting.

Final checklist before sync
- [ ] Choose 1 claim to deep-dive and attach one-pager
- [ ] Send one-pager 24h before (if more than 1 item needs review)
- [ ] Add direct evidence links (dashboard, pilot email)
- [ ] Write the one-line ask and preferred timeline

Quick backlog of future claims (brainstorm)
- Template: "X by Y via Z" e.g., "Reduce inference flakiness by 20% by end of Q2 via circuit-breaker and health-check rollout."
- Bring these to 1:many manager syncs only when top 3 are stable.

End notes: keep this doc as living scratch. After the sync, copy the one-pager to PeopleOps shared folder and update my personal status board.
